name: Improved Biomass Cooking Systems
summary: Efficient cookstoves and kilns that reduce biomass consumption by 40–60% compared to traditional three-stone fires, cutting fuel costs, indoor air pollution, and deforestation pressure.
description: Improved biomass cooking systems encompass a range of technologies that convert woody biomass, agricultural residues, and charcoal with higher thermal efficiency than traditional three-stone fires or simple mud stoves. Technologies deployed in Uganda include rocket stoves, gasifier stoves, briquette stoves, and improved kilns for fish smoking and food processing. In agricultural settings, improved biomass systems are used for crop drying, food processing, tea curing, and institutional cooking. These systems can achieve 40–60% reductions in fuel consumption compared to traditional methods. In fishing communities, improved fish smoking kilns (such as the Chorkor kiln) dramatically reduce wood consumption and improve product quality. Biomass briquettes from agricultural waste (groundnut shells, rice husks, sugarcane bagasse) offer an alternative to wood fuel and reduce pressure on forest resources.
applications: Household cooking energy in rural areas
Tea and crop drying in agro-processing
benefits: Significant reduction in indoor air pollution and health risks
Reduces household expenditure on firewood and charcoal
Technologies can be fabricated locally using available materials
Briquette-based systems provide market for agricultural waste
limitations: Technology adoption can be slow due to user behavioural preferences
Performance depends on stove-user combination (requires training)
Biomass availability and quality affects performance
Limited impact without addressing underlying fuelwood supply
Some improved stoves perform poorly with charcoal fuel
operationalNotes: Train users on correct lighting technique for maximum efficiency
Use dry, well-seasoned wood for best results
Ensure pots fit correctly on stove — poorly fitted pots waste heat
Community demonstration and peer exchange accelerates adoption
Pair stove distribution with household energy awareness campaigns
maintenanceNotes: Inspect combustion chamber for cracks or damage seasonally
Replace ceramic liner in rocket stoves every 2–3 years
Clean grate and ash chamber weekly
Repaint external metal surfaces annually for improved kilns
Provide users with simple repair kit and basic maintenance training
